proves.claim: A lease lapses strictly after its end, and a lease lasts two minutes by default.

jobs.lease.lapse-boundary.why: A lease that lapsed a tick early let two drivers hold one job.

proves.claim: takeJob gives the lease to one driver, refuses a second while it is live, and gives it over once it lapsed.

jobs.lease.take-one-driver.why: Two drivers could both be given the same live job.

proves.claim: Only the holder renews a live lease, and a lapsed lease cannot be renewed.

jobs.lease.holder-renews.why: A non-holder renewing a lease would steal a job.

proves.claim: reclaimLapsed names each lapsed lease with how long ago it ended, oldest first, and leaves live leases alone.

jobs.lease.reclaim-oldest-first.why: Reclaiming in the wrong order starved the longest-lapsed job.

proves.claim: releaseLease frees the lease for its holder only.

jobs.lease.release-holder-only.why: Any driver could free another driver's lease.

proves.claim: finishJob marks the job done for its holder or an unleased or lapsed job, but not against a live rival.

jobs.lease.finish-holder-only.why: A finish against a live rival lease marked a job done under its owner.

proves.claim: A job released with a backoff still reads as the step it kept, with its lease freed.

jobs.lease.backoff-keeps-step.why: A release with backoff lost the step the job had reached.

proves.claim: On macOS the lander wake runs as a launchd job, so launchd is its parent and responsible process; a later launch boots the finished job out.

jobs.launch.launchd-wake.why: A lander wake launched from a runner without launchd ownership died with its parent.

proves.claim: On a fixture board with no launchd option the job is a plain detached spawn and the launchd job count is unchanged.

jobs.launch.fixture-plain-spawn.why: Test runs left hundreds of launchd jobs loaded that no later sweep could see.

proves.claim: On a fixture board an explicit launchd: true still starts the job through the launcher's bootstrap.

jobs.launch.fixture-declared-launchd.why: A declared launchd start must keep working for the launchd-wake proof.

proves.claim: Without launchd the process is a plain detached spawn that still writes its log.

jobs.launch.plain-spawn-log.why: Without launchd the job's log went missing.

proves.claim: When the gui bootstrap fails the plain spawn runs the job and reports launchd false.

jobs.launch.bootstrap-fails-fallback.why: A failed gui bootstrap left the job unrun.

proves.claim: A runner with no gui session still runs the job, whatever launchctl answers.

jobs.launch.no-gui-session.why: A runner with no gui session never ran the job.

proves.claim: The job file escapes its strings and runs the command once.

jobs.launch.job-file-escapes.why: An unescaped string in the job file broke the launchd job.

proves.claim: A review job is named by its item, and a bad item or reviewer is refused.

jobs.review.named-by-item.why: A bad item or reviewer id made a malformed review job.

proves.claim: reserveReview gives the review to one reviewer and names the holder to a second.

jobs.review.reserve-one-reviewer.why: Two reviewers could take the same review.

proves.claim: renewReview extends the holder's reservation only.

jobs.review.renew-holder-only.why: A non-holder could extend a review reservation.

proves.claim: A lapsed reservation is reclaimed with a lapsed step and offered again, and a fresh sighting of the reviewer extends it instead.

jobs.review.lapsed-reclaimed.why: A lapsed reservation was never offered again, or a live reviewer lost theirs.

proves.claim: releaseReview frees a held review and says who held it, and answers null when nobody did.

jobs.review.release-names-holder.why: A release did not say who held the review.

proves.claim: reviewOffer offers an item nobody holds and names the live holder otherwise.

jobs.review.offer-names-holder.why: An item held by a live reviewer was offered to others.

proves.claim: SM5: releaseReview releases a live holder, then marks the review job done; a lapsed or missing job ends without a released step.

jobs.review.release-marks-done.why: A released review stayed open instead of done.

proves.claim: SM5: reclaimLapsedReviews never extends a lease whose item is not submitted, however fresh the heartbeat.

jobs.review.reclaim-needs-submitted.why: A fresh heartbeat extended a lease on an item no longer submitted.

proves.claim: createJob stores a queued job once, and creating an id that exists returns the stored job unchanged.

jobs.store.create-once.why: Creating a job twice replaced the stored job.

proves.claim: nameJob fills what a job lacked and never moves a named job onto another candidate.

jobs.store.name-fills-only.why: Naming a job could move it onto another candidate.

proves.claim: writeStep appends in order, the current step is the last written, and a repeat of the same key writes nothing.

jobs.store.step-append-order.why: Steps were reordered or repeated rows were written.

proves.claim: writeStep inside the caller's transaction joins it and rolls back with it.

jobs.store.step-joins-transaction.why: A step written inside a caller's transaction survived its rollback.

proves.claim: jobView is null for an unknown job, and jobsOf lists one kind oldest first, optionally for one item.

jobs.store.views-and-lists.why: jobView and jobsOf answered wrongly for unknown jobs or item filters.

proves.claim: leasedJobs lists only a kind's jobs with a live lease that are not done.

jobs.store.leased-live-only.why: Done or unleased jobs were listed as leased.

proves.claim: The claim query reads job through an index on its step and never scans job_step.

jobs.claim-plan.index-no-scan.why: A claim scanned job_step and slowed every runner.

proves.claim: The board API answers a health request within 1 s while runners claim from a 33k-row job table.

jobs.claim-plan.health-under-load.why: The board API stalled while runners claimed from a large job table.

proves.claim: A receipt with a plan carries files, tiers, phase plan, check, counts, log and its recorded receipts.

jobs.gate-receipt.plan-fields.why: A receipt lost its files, tiers or plan.

proves.claim: A red phase names its own log, and a log name that is a path is never joined.

jobs.gate-receipt.red-phase-log.why: A path-like log name was joined into a path.

proves.claim: A 0.9.3 receipt without plan, counts or kept logs reads as it was, with no added fields.

jobs.gate-receipt.old-receipt.why: An older receipt gained fields it never had.

proves.claim: A receipt id is a fixed 36-character id per job and phase.

jobs.gate-receipt.id-fixed-width.why: Receipt ids varied in length per job and phase.

proves.claim: A runner claims the highest priority class first: interactive, gate, landing, then background.

jobs.priority.class-order.why: A background job was claimed ahead of an interactive one.

proves.claim: A class with a reserve still gets its reserved slot under full load.

jobs.priority.reserved-slot.why: A class with a reserve starved under full load.

proves.claim: With no priority setting the claim order is unchanged: landings, then test and main-test runs by age, then the rest by age.

jobs.priority.default-order.why: With no priority setting the claim order changed.

proves.claim: The claim scan orders and limits job ids first, then reads payloads only for the rows it returns, in the order it had before.

jobs.priority.ids-first.why: Every offered payload went through the claim scan's sorter and held the board lock for seconds.

proves.claim: With an older gate-shard row and a newer main-test row offered, the plain order offers the main-test row first.

jobs.priority.main-test-before-shards.why: Main-test runs waited behind the whole gate-shard backlog while finished items sat unsettled.

proves.claim: A land row still comes before a main-test row.

jobs.priority.land-still-first.why: Ranking main-test beside test could have put it ahead of a landing.

proves.claim: With 600 offered rows whose payloads exceed 40 KB, the runnable filter, push-first order and reserve order are unchanged.

jobs.priority.ids-first-filter.why: Moving the payload read after the limit could have changed which rows a claim saw or their order.

proves.claim: A queued job older than its kind limit with no waiter is expired with a recorded reason.

jobs.expire.queued-over-limit.why: Old queued jobs with no waiter stayed queued forever.

proves.claim: A running or leased-queued gate whose lease lapsed reads stalled with its age in minutes, and a driven one does not.

jobs.panel.stalled-gate.why: A gate with a lapsed lease read as running.

proves.claim: gatePanel and stalledGates read the board: unknown job and missing tables answer nothing, stalled gates are listed.

jobs.panel.reads-board.why: Missing job tables crashed the gate panel.

proves.claim: A submit handoff is shadowed as a gate job whose steps repeat per state, and a board without job tables refuses.

jobs.panel.submit-shadow.why: A submit handoff left no gate job to show.

proves.claim: Gate spans append to a file per day under the common dir, and reading returns those in range, skipping torn and foreign lines.

jobs.panel.spans-per-day.why: Gate spans were lost or torn lines broke reading.

proves.claim: A new day's first span removes day files older than the 14-day window.

jobs.panel.span-retention.why: Old day files were never removed.

proves.claim: every jobs-cell test registered here has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

jobs.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: Every jobs test file that reads repo files carries an input header naming the cells it reads.

jobs.inputs.readers-declare-headers.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: No jobs test declares the whole source tree except the existing ones, and every header names cells or files.

jobs.inputs.no-whole-tree-header.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: With a write hold set through setWriteHold, atomically() calls prepare, begin, then finish with released after COMMIT or rolled-back after ROLLBACK, in that order.

jobs.store.hold-port-brackets-write.why: Without it the board api's job writes never reach the write-holder markers.

proves.claim: An atomically() call nested inside a caller's transaction calls none of the write hold's functions.

jobs.store.hold-port-skips-savepoint.why: Without it a nested write would record a second marker for one board write.

proves.claim: atomically on a handle with busy_timeout 0 waits for a board another connection releases within the bound, runs its work, and commits.

jobs.store.busy-retries-then-succeeds.why: A job write on a briefly held board crashed with a raw database is locked error.

proves.claim: With the board held past the bound, atomically throws Refused BOARD_BUSY, leaves no open transaction and restores the handle busy_timeout.

jobs.store.busy-surfaces-board-busy.why: A held board surfaced a raw SQLITE error and left the handle changed.

proves.claim: The createJob then writeStep sequence run inside atomically on a held board throws BOARD_BUSY and writes nothing.

jobs.store.offer-sequence-busy.why: offerJob crashed with ERR_SQLITE_ERROR when the board stayed busy.
